author: i. a. short
title: Rep. Troy Nehls votes to send Secure America Act to President Trump's desk
text:
Congressman Troy E. Nehls announced on June 9 that he voted in favor of S.2, the Secure America Act, which aims to provide increased funding for federal law enforcement agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement and U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and supports efforts by the Trump Administration to secure national borders.
Nehls said, “Because Democrats in Congress have refused to fund our brave ICE officers and Border Patrol Agents through regular order, my Republican colleagues and I in both the House and Senate have worked tirelessly to robustly fund these agencies through September 30, 2029, ensuring that Democrats’ political games cannot further hamstring the security of our homeland.” He added that the legislation invests in advanced technology intended to help federal law enforcement mitigate threats at U.S. borders.
“While Democrats continue to fight to defund law enforcement and abolish ICE, my Republican colleagues and I stand united in ensuring that ICE officers and Border Patrol Agents have the support they need to keep America safe,” Nehls said.
Troy Nehls is currently serving in the U.S. Congress representing Texas’ 22nd district after replacing Pete Olson in 2021; he has held this seat since then, according to official congressional records . In recent elections for this district, Nehls defeated Jamie Jordan in 2022 with approximately 62 percent of the vote, Marquette Greene-Scott in 2024 with about 62 percent of the vote as well, and Sri Preston Kulkarni in 2020 with just over half of all votes cast, according to official election results .
Nehls was born in Beaver Dam, Wisconsin in 1968 and currently resides in Richmond, according to his biography .
